Ashwin: Heads up — spotted an odd pattern in KV during a long session repro: residency drops ~20% mid-session and eviction counters spike briefly, then back to normal. Seems correlated with large batched requests. @Maya any idea? :eyes:
Maya: Hmm can you paste the timeline + the profile? is this on a dedicated node or hosted?
Ashwin: Dedicated pool (type-d4). Timeline: 11:12:03 --> steady residency ~92%, 11:15:10 eviction-count spikes for ~30s, residency dips to ~72%, hit_rate drops. No deploys at that time. Attach Prometheus slices below.
Leo: Could be fragmentation + a GC-ish compaction path. Do we have eviction_reason labels?
Ashwin: Yes, eviction_reason shows "memory_pressure" and some "stale_key". Eviction age histogram skewed to <5s.
Maya: Can you share the prom queries you used?
Ashwin: PromQL snippets I used: ```
sum by(instance) (increase(kv_evictions_total[1m]))
sum by(instance) (kv_residency_percentile{quantile="0.95"})
avg_over_time(kv_hit_rate[5m])
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(kv_eviction_age_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
Ashwin: Also grabbed a pprof CPU+heap around the spike — attaching snapshot link in thread.
Sara: Quick thought — batching heuristics can create short bursts of new keys leading to page chain churn. Did you check whether the requests during the spike had unusually high prefix churn?
Ashwin: Yes, request-level key cardinality jumped x3 for ~20s. KV-store shows increased page splits in audit log.
Maya: If page splits are happening, reuse will drop and fragmentation increases. We should track "kv_page_splits_total" and a "kv_compactable_fragments" gauge. Can we add those to the dashboard?
Leo: Agreed. Also add a rolling metric for "residency_streaks" (consecutive seconds below threshold) — could help alert on transient dips.
kv-monitor-bot: new metric scraped: kv_page_splits_total -> value 42 at 2026-04-08T11:15:20Z
Ashwin: Proposed quick triage steps: 1) add kv_page_splits_total and kv_fragmentation_ratio to the per-node dashboard; 2) instrument eviction_reason breakdown per shard; 3) add a short-running sampler that collects a single pprof when eviction spikes > 10/s for >10s.
Maya: Also check kernel selection side — if a compiled path falls back (e.g., non-optimized matmul path), we sometimes see memory pattern changes due to different allocation sizes. Not likely but worth keeping an eye.
Leo: For observability, I can add a panel showing eviction_age histogram alongside top-5 keys churn rate. That should show if short-lived keys are dominating evictions.
Ashwin: I'm going to run a controlled load where we replay the exact batched workload and toggle batching window from 5ms -> 20ms to see sensitivity. Will post results.
Sara: If reproduction is easy, we can try a patch that delays page splits by coalescing small inserts for 10ms and see effect. Might reduce latency? risky but low-effort in a staging branch.
Maya: Nice. Also create an alerting rule: if 95p residency drops >10% while eviction_rate > 5/s for 30s, page the oncall.
Ashwin: Added an investigation card in the runtime board and linked the pprof. Will update after the replay. Thanks all :thumbsup:
